note: Concept cards: our own explanations, linked to curriculum chapters. This is the RAG corpus - the tutor teaches FROM these, not from model memory.

cards.title: Real Numbers: HCF and LCM by Prime Factorisation
cards.explanation: Every number above 1 breaks into a product of primes. HCF takes the SMALLEST power of each COMMON prime; LCM takes the BIGGEST power of each prime that appears. HCF x LCM = product of the two numbers (works for two numbers only).
misconceptions: taking the biggest power for HCF (that gives LCM)
applying HCF x LCM = product to three numbers

cards.title: Zeroes of a Polynomial
cards.explanation: A zero of p(x) is the x-value where the polynomial equals zero - the graph crosses the x-axis. For a quadratic ax^2 + bx + c, the sum of zeroes is -b/a and the product is c/a, even before you solve it.
cards.worked_example: p(x) = x^2 - 5x + 6. Sum of zeroes = -(-5)/1 = 5, product = 6/1 = 6. Indeed the zeroes are 2 and 3: 2 + 3 = 5, 2 x 3 = 6.
misconceptions: using b/a instead of -b/a for the sum
thinking a zero means the polynomial is undefined there

cards.title: Solving Two Linear Equations: Substitution and Elimination
cards.explanation: Two equations, two unknowns: express one variable in terms of the other (substitution) or add/subtract scaled equations so one variable cancels (elimination). One solution = lines intersect; no solution = parallel; infinite solutions = same line.
cards.worked_example: x + y = 7 and x - y = 3. Add them: 2x = 10, so x = 5. Then y = 7 - 5 = 2.
misconceptions: adding equations without matching coefficients first
losing the minus sign when subtracting an entire equation

cards.title: Solving Quadratics by Splitting the Middle Term
cards.explanation: For x^2 + bx + c, find two numbers that MULTIPLY to c and ADD to b. Split the middle term using them, group in pairs, pull out common factors. For ax^2 with a not 1, split using two numbers whose product is a x c and sum is b.
cards.worked_example: x^2 - 5x + 6: need product 6, sum -5 -> the numbers -2 and -3. So x^2 - 2x - 3x + 6 = x(x - 2) - 3(x - 2) = (x - 2)(x - 3). Zeroes: x = 2, x = 3.
misconceptions: finding numbers that add to c instead of multiplying to c
forgetting BOTH signs flip when c is positive but b is negative

cards.title: The Discriminant: Predicting Root Types
cards.explanation: For ax^2 + bx + c = 0, D = b^2 - 4ac decides everything: D > 0 gives two distinct real roots, D = 0 gives one repeated root, D < 0 gives no real roots. Compute D BEFORE solving - it tells you what to expect.
misconceptions: computing b^2 - 4ac as (b - 4a)(b + 4ac)
claiming D < 0 means x = 0

cards.title: Arithmetic Progression: nth Term
cards.explanation: An AP adds the same common difference d each step. The nth term is a_n = a + (n - 1)d, where a is the first term. Count terms carefully: from a_3 to a_10 there are 7 steps, not 8.
misconceptions: using n x d instead of (n - 1) x d
counting the first term as a step

cards.title: Similar Triangles: AA, SSS, SAS
cards.explanation: Similar triangles have the same shape: angles equal and sides in proportion. AA (two angles match) is enough because the third angle follows. SSS needs all three side RATIOS equal; SAS needs two side ratios equal AND the angle between them.
cards.worked_example: If angle A = angle D and angle B = angle E, then triangle ABC ~ triangle DEF by AA, so AB/DE = BC/EF = AC/DF.
misconceptions: using SAS with the angle NOT between the two sides
thinking equal sides means similar but proportional means congruent (it is the reverse)

cards.title: Distance Formula
cards.explanation: Distance between (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) is sqrt((x2 - x1)^2 + (y2 - y1)^2) - it is Pythagoras on the grid. Subtract in the same order both times; squaring hides sign mistakes but (x2 - x1) with (y1 - y2) mixes order and can still work only because of squaring - be consistent anyway.
misconceptions: adding before squaring: sqrt((x2 + x1)^2)
mixing subtraction order between x and y pairs

cards.title: Trigonometric Ratios in a Right Triangle
cards.explanation: For an angle in a right triangle: sin = opposite/hypotenuse, cos = adjacent/hypotenuse, tan = opposite/adjacent (remember SOH-CAH-TOA). Standard values worth memorising: sin 30 = 1/2, cos 60 = 1/2, tan 45 = 1, sin 45 = cos 45 = 1/sqrt(2).
cards.worked_example: In a right triangle with hypotenuse 10 and angle 30 at A, the side opposite A = 10 x sin 30 = 10 x 1/2 = 5.
misconceptions: swapping opposite and adjacent relative to the chosen angle
using sin 45 = 1/2 (that is sin 30)

cards.title: Mean of Grouped Data
cards.explanation: For grouped data, multiply each class midpoint x_i by its frequency f_i, add them, divide by total frequency: mean = sum(f_i x x_i) / sum(f_i). The midpoint is (lower limit + upper limit)/2.
misconceptions: using class limits instead of midpoints
dividing by the number of classes instead of total frequency

cards.title: Basic Probability
cards.explanation: P(event) = favourable outcomes / total outcomes, always between 0 and 1. P(not E) = 1 - P(E). Count the TOTAL carefully - for two dice there are 36 outcomes, not 12.
misconceptions: counting 6 x 2 = 12 outcomes for two dice
adding probabilities of events that can happen together

cards.title: Operations on Rational Numbers
cards.explanation: Add fractions by first making denominators equal (LCM), then adding numerators. Multiply straight across: top x top, bottom x bottom. Divide by flipping the second fraction and multiplying.
misconceptions: adding denominators directly: 2/3 + 1/4 = 3/7 (wrong)
flipping the FIRST fraction when dividing

cards.title: Solving Linear Equations in One Variable
cards.explanation: Keep the equation balanced: do the same operation to both sides. Move variable terms to one side, numbers to the other, then divide. Always substitute your answer back to check.
misconceptions: adding 5 to both sides instead of subtracting
dividing only one term by the coefficient

cards.title: Finding Square Roots by Prime Factorisation
cards.explanation: Break the number into primes and pair identical factors; the square root takes ONE from each pair. Any factor left unpaired stays under the root sign.
misconceptions: taking one from only some pairs
forgetting unpaired factors remain inside the root

cards.title: Percentage Increase and Decrease
cards.explanation: Percentage change = (new - old)/old x 100. A 20% increase followed by a 20% decrease does NOT return to the start - the second 20% acts on a bigger number.
cards.worked_example: Rs 250 increased by 20%: 250 + 50 = 300. Decreased by 20%: 300 - 60 = 240, which is below 250.
misconceptions: assuming percentage up then down cancels out
computing change from the NEW value instead of the old
